task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: regression to the mean and score-state confounding
methodological_questions: Is the between-team variance in the defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change larger than game-level sampling noise?
Does the effect persist across split halves of a season and across seasons?
Does the effect survive control for opponent H1 level, score state, garbage time, and opponent and venue?
Does a placebo or permutation null calibrate the reliability estimate?

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of connector teammate-path quality was low (r=+0.215, Spearman-Brown about 0.355, ICC 0.216 with 78.4% within-player variance, n=102). [prior work] concludes it is too low to treat as a stable scoutable trait. Limiting factor: low measurement reliability.

Playsheet validation after defenses dropped a play type by 0.25 PPP or more from H1 to H2 showed no clear full-rank signal (Spearman rho=-0.0639, p=0.0997, n=665). BEST beat AVOID pairwise (1.257 vs 1.092, p=0.004). [prior work] lists leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample, and drift as limits.
An apparent rise in opponent PPP after a star's second foul (+0.204) came from a free-throw share mismatch (41.8% vs 9.9%). After matching it was +0.049 and not significant.

The Possession Control Index gain over ORtg was leakage tracking DRtg (corr +0.894), because the baseline omitted defense by construction. The n=120 team-seasons sample was used there, with a 2025-26 out-of-sample set of 30 teams.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a half-to-half on-off quality metric as a stable trait
failed_approaches.why: Low measurement reliability: most variance was within-unit from one half to the other (A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using H1-to-H2 defensive drops to predict which counter works in H2, with a full-rank test
failed_approaches.why: Limited by leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample, and drift; mechanism unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A defense-proxy metric tested against an outcome (Net Rating) that contains defense by construction
Raw opponent PPP comparison that included free throws
failed_approaches.why: Construction artifact: the treated and control groups had different free-throw shares (C_artifact).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests whether a defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.
Earlier work found that half-to-half split-half reliability of derived on-off or defense metrics can be low ([prior work][prior work]).
Earlier H1-to-H2 defensive-drop designs were inconclusive and exposed to leakage and drift ([prior work][prior work]).
Earlier work recorded two artifact mechanisms that apply here: outcome-derived or mechanical construction, and mismatched composition between groups (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the between-team variance in opponent H2-H1 change attributable to defense is nonzero.
The size of the year-to-year or split-half reliability of this specific team trait.
Whether any such trait is independent of overall defensive quality or of the opponent's own H1 level.
Whether the 120 team-seasons give adequate power for a reliability estimate.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 change is a difference score, so its noise is higher than that of either half alone. Mean reversion in H1 level (a high opponent H1 predicts a negative change) is likely to dominate the raw measure.
Team-level reliability is likely to be low. Game-level H2-H1 noise is large relative to plausible true between-team differences, and the earlier split-half results point the same way.
Garbage time, blowout rotations, and starter minutes can change H2 for reasons unrelated to defensive suppression, so they must be modelled.
The question is testable as a reliability or variance-component question, even though a positive effect is unlikely to be detectable at 120 team-seasons.
Stated for later reference: a defense that is strong overall will show up as a trait in H1 and H2 alike, which could be mislabelled as an H2-H1 effect unless the baseline is controlled.
uncertainties: The distribution of game-level H2-H1 noise in these data is unseen.
It is not known whether H1 and H2 possession counts are balanced across games.
2025-26 playoff data may be partial or complete depending on the analysis date; regular-season and playoff samples are small or heterogeneous.
No retrieved record addresses halftime adjustment by the opponent versus by the defense.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records on low split-half reliability ([prior work][prior work]) and on mechanical, leakage, and composition artifacts (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) moved the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes. The changes are a variance-component reliability design, residualisation on H1, leakage-free baselines, and placebo and permutation nulls. No record answers the question directly, so the evidence only shaped the risk assessment.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 120 team-seasons (30 teams over 4 seasons) are available. Per-game H2-H1 noise is large, so only a moderate or large true between-team variance can be detected.

The H2-H1 difference score is inherently noisy. Split-half reliability may be too low to call the effect a trait, and low reliability of derived team metrics has been recorded before ([prior work][prior work]).
Opponent H1 level is negatively tied to H2-H1 change by construction, so a mean-reversion artifact can mimic or hide a defense effect.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study answers this question. Related records show low split-half reliability of derived metrics, inconclusive H1-to-H2 defensive-drop validation, and artifact risks from mechanical construction and composition mismatch.

risks.text: Opponent H2-H1 change is mechanically negatively related to opponent H1 performance. Defenses that suppress H1 will appear to have positive H2-H1 effects. Control for H1 level or use out-of-sample baselines.
The difference score has low signal-to-noise. Report split-half and cross-season reliability with confidence intervals and Spearman-Brown corrections.
120 team-seasons gives limited power for a variance-component estimate. Pre-specify the minimum detectable ICC.
Score state, garbage time, opponent offense quality, home or away, rest, starter minutes, and fatigue can all drive H2-H1 change independently of the defense.
Defense quality and baselines must be built without H2 of the games being scored, and without using the outcome. [prior work][prior work] recorded leakage through a metric that tracks DRtg.
Defining the 'effect' from the same H2-H1 outcome that is then tested for reliability can produce circularity. Use independent game subsets for estimation and evaluation.
Rosters, trades, injuries, and rule or style changes across 2022-26 may break persistence. A cross-season correlation may be low even if the trait exists within a season.
Reliability must be calibrated against a permutation null that shuffles team labels within opponent strata. Otherwise noise-driven correlations look like traits.
Multiple outcomes (PPP, points, eFG), splits, and season pairs would inflate false positives unless one primary is fixed.

design.estimand: Between-team variance (ICC, reliability) of a defense's causal effect on opponent H2-H1 change in points per 100 possessions. The change is residualised on the opponent's expected H2-H1 change given opponent H1 level, opponent identity or strength, venue, and rest. Primary reliability metrics: (a) odd/even game split-half correlation within season with Spearman-Brown correction, and (b) year-to-year correlation across consecutive seasons, with a mixed-model variance share as support.
design.unit: Team-season defense (primary) with game as the repeated measure; team-season is the analysis unit for reliability.
design.sample: All 120 team-seasons from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (30 teams x 4 seasons). Primary analysis excludes playoffs and any partial 2025-26 data. Exclude games after a 20+ point lead is reached (garbage time) as the primary rule, and report all games as a sensitivity analysis. Playoff data is exploratory only.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, compute the minimum detectable ICC or split-half r given the observed game-level noise SD and about 80 games per team-season. Report a simulation for 120 team-seasons at true reliabilities of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. If power to detect r=0.3 is below 0.8, label a null as inconclusive rather than rejected.
design.controls: Opponent H1 PPP and its season baseline (to remove regression to the mean), opponent offensive rating, home/away, rest days, score margin at halftime, starters' H2 minutes, pace, and the defense's own overall quality. Baselines are built from prior games only, with no use of the scored game's H2. Estimate team effects with a mixed model with random team effects and fixed opponent effects. Use separate game subsets for estimating effects and evaluating persistence.
design.falsification: (1) Permutation null: shuffle defense labels within opponent-strength strata 10,000 times and compare observed reliability to the null. (2) Placebo: apply the same procedure to H1-to-Q-split changes with no halftime break (Q1 to Q2), and to a random game split with no defensive attribution. (3) Negative control: apply the method to the team's own offense H2-H1 change. (4) Check that the result is not simply overall defensive rating by adding it as a covariate. The claim is supported only if the reliability exceeds the permutation null and survives the covariates.
design.multiplicity: One primary: odd/even split-half reliability of PPP-based H2-H1 effect after residualisation, pooled over seasons. Cross-season persistence is a single pre-specified secondary. Everything else is exploratory with Holm correction at alpha=0.05.
design.decision_rule: Supported (trait): primary reliability >= 0.30 with the 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0, permutation p < 0.05, and the result surviving the overall-defense control and the Q1-Q2 placebo. Rejected: the 95% CI upper bound is below 0.30 and power to detect r=0.30 is at least 0.8. Otherwise inconclusive. Reject if the effect appears only in raw H2-H1 and vanishes after residualising on H1 (artifact).
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type possession graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, as complete on 2026-10-06 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13). Freeze a snapshot with a hash before analysis; 2025-26 playoffs held as an untouched confirmation set.
